title: Curio example prompt fixture (v1)
description: One reviewed, checked-in pairing of a natural-language prompt with a shipped example dataflow, used by the example-derived agent validation harness (memo dev/121, DEC-077). The evaluated model receives `prompt` (and `context`) and nothing else: `expected`, `required`, `intents` and `source` are the harness's answer key and must never be sent to it. The format is also the fine-tuning export unit -- `split` and `review` govern that, and held-out fixtures are never training data.

fixtureId.description: Stable id; the example's file stem (curated) or its basename without .json (legacy).

version.description: Fixture format revision; bump when the meaning of a field changes.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the example this fixture describes.

sha256.description: Digest of that file. A drift guard: an example edit fails the unit suite until a human re-reviews the fixture.

walkthrough.description: The companion Markdown, when the example has one.

prompt.description: What a person would type. Must leak no implementation: no node or edge id, no canonical template id, no line of node content, no plan-grammar token, no JSON. Human node-kind names ("Data Transformation", "Vega-Lite") are fine -- the walkthroughs use them.

context.description: Optional second turn-level context string, sent verbatim with the prompt.

required.description: The dependency source of truth, copied from the example's own dataflow.datasets and dataflow.packages (dev/81, dev/101), plus repo-relative paths for the legacy examples that still read a committed file.

paths.description: Repo-relative data files the prompt must name verbatim (the DEC-072 user-typed-path route).

expected.description: The example, normalized. Recomputed and compared by the unit suite -- never hand-edited into disagreement with the source file.

ref.description: Harness-local handle. Never sent to the model; the runtime mints its own refs and ids.

executable.description: Whether the sandbox can run this kind (derived per DEC-076; informational in the fixture).

slot.description: Merge-flow input index parsed from targetHandle in_N; null for a single-input port.

sources.description: What the example's node code actually reads, scanned with the production grounding regexes -- the fabrication baseline.

intents.description: Per-node meaning checks. `mustMention` matches case-insensitively against the reconstructed node's goal/intent text; `outputKind` against the kind Solve recorded (absent -> notMeasured, excluded from the score's denominator).

slotOrderMatters.description: Set on a merge target whose input order changes the result; otherwise slot mismatches on that node are not penalised.

mode.description: sandbox: Solve can verify the executable nodes. browser: the graph only runs in the page (grammars, widgets). none: nothing is executed.

browserOnlyKinds.description: Canonical types excluded from the execution score because they render in the browser.

tier.description: T0 offline and fully expressible; T1 needs a reviewed local install; T2 needs a contract capability this branch lacks; T3 needs the network or hardware.

needs.description: package-enlist:templates and package-enlist:dependencies are DIFFERENT routes: a template the plan cannot name until the package is enlisted, versus a library the node code imports whose owning manifest declares it. Neither justifies authoring a package.

skip.description: Every exclusion is visible and justified. An empty list means the fixture always runs.

when.description: The condition, e.g. "!CURIO_EVAL_EXTERNAL" or a `needs` entry.

thresholds.description: Per-fixture bars. Dimension weights are harness constants, not fixture data.

split.description: Fine-tuning export split. Immutable once approved; a heldout fixture is never training data (DEC-077).

review.description: A model may draft a prompt from the example and its walkthrough as a one-time authoring aid; a human reviews and commits it. The deterministic suite does not depend on the review; the live report labels it; the export refuses anything not approved.

consent.description: What a training or evaluation export of this fixture would carry, and under which licence (memo dev/122). Declared rather than assumed: `OQ-010`'s recorded posture treats unclassified context as ineligible for remote egress, so a fixture is eligible for a fine-tuning upload only while `dataContent` is `identifiers-only`. Absent means the shipped corpus's default, and a test asserts every shipped fixture declares it explicitly.

dataContent.description: `identifiers-only`: the row carries the prompt, the expected graph shape and the plan text plus dataset and package IDENTIFIERS — no dataset row, column, geometry or file. `user-content`: the row would carry content a person authored in their own dataflow, which needs its own consent surface and is refused by the training-set builder until it has one.

licence.description: The licence the authored parts of this fixture are under.

sourceLicences.description: The licences of the datasets this fixture NAMES, recorded so a reader can see they were considered. They are not implicated by an export that carries identifiers only.
